title: Magnets
_map: Magnets (stretch, usually Y3). Big idea: magnets attract some metals; poles push and pull. Creative: find what sticks around the farm; design a magnet-powered gate.
_story: Steve dropped a box of bits in the hay. It uses a magnet to fish them out, but not everything comes. Then two magnets push each other away, and Steve is amazed.
_stepChain: a magnet pulls some things → paper clips and spoons: yes; wood, plastic: no → not every metal (foil, most coins) → magnets have two ends called poles → same poles push apart, opposite poles pull together → design a gate

talk.ask: Does a magnet pick up every metal?
talk.goodAnswer: no: iron and steel things like paper clips, but not foil or most coins.

talk.ask: What happens when you put two magnets' same ends together?
talk.goodAnswer: they push each other apart. Opposite ends pull together.

handsOn: Take a fridge magnet on a hunt round the house. What sticks? What doesn't? If you have two magnets, feel them push and pull.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I dropped my bits and bobs in the hay! I'll use my magnet to fish them out.

question.prompt: Which things do you think the magnet will pull?
question.reveal: Only some metal things! The paper clip and the spoon zoom over. The wood and plastic stay put. And so does the foil, even though it's metal.

narration.text: Magnets pull things that contain iron or steel, like paper clips, spoons and nails. Other metals, like the foil, aren't pulled at all.
Every magnet has two ends, called poles: a north pole and a south pole. Put a north pole next to a south pole, and they pull together, click!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Now I'll turn one magnet round, so two north poles face each other. They'll pull together even harder!

question.prompt: What will two north poles do?
question.onRight: Yes. The same poles push each other away. You can feel it, like an invisible cushion.

0.hint: Opposite poles pull. What about poles that are the same?
0.say: Opposite poles pull together, but the same poles push apart. Two norths push each other away.

question.reveal: Same poles push apart. Opposite poles pull together.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Can you design a gate that shuts itself with magnets? Maybe a magnet on the gate and a metal plate on the post. Draw it and tell a grown-up!

rule.text: Magnets pull iron. Same poles push, opposite poles pull.
rule.ask: Can you say what happens when two magnets meet? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Magnets pull things made of iron or steel. Opposite poles pull together, and the same poles push apart.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: a compass needle is a tiny magnet. Why does it always point the same way?
choices: The Earth is like a giant magnet
bonus.reveal: The Earth is like a giant magnet, and the needle lines up with it, pointing north.
